problem: Rewrite the expression $({y}^{2}+12y+{6}^{2})-3$ as the difference between a perfect square and a constant.

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{y}^{2}+2ay+{a}^{2}=(y+a{)}^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+20y+{10}^{2} & = \\ {y}^{2}+2\cdot 10y+{10}^{2} & = \\ (y+10{)}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}^{2}+20y+{10}^{2})+7 & = \\ (y+10{)}^{2}+7 & .\end{aligned}
$$
